score.product: AUTOMATED INSULIN DOSING DEVICE SYSTEM, SINGLE HORMONAL CONTROL
score.rationale: Hypoglycemia is the very risk these automated insulin delivery systems are designed to prevent; reports reflect lack of efficacy (device failing to prevent the indication event), not a new injury. The PRR is declining (slope -3.69) and reflects background noise. Class III PMA device faces Riegel preemption. Even if a parallel claim existed (software malfunction, manufacturing defect), the high case volume (5630) and established literature suggest the risk is known and labeled. This is a pass: no duty to warn that insulin therapy may fail to control glucose.

score.rationale: This is classic indication confounding. Leflunomide is prescribed for rheumatoid arthritis, and anti-CCP antibodies are a diagnostic marker for RA, not a drug-induced injury. The signal reflects the drug being used in patients who already have RA (and thus are anti-CCP positive), not the drug causing the antibodies. The extreme PRRs (600+) collapsing to zero confirm this is artifact. Generic availability (36 ANDAs) further preempts claims. Viability is zero.
